guard_streams.write_limit: Switching process guidance is not physical coverage, live orderability or selected-parcel performance evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the switching overview on 13 August 2021.
The page was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Mobile customers can switch using a free text process.
Broadband customers can use One Touch Switch.
Landline customers can use One Touch Switch.
The new provider arranges broadband and landline switches.
Ofcom provides separate guides for mobile, broadband and landline.
The mobile guide explains Text to Switch.
The broadband guide explains One Touch Switch.
The page links guidance for customers whose provider goes out of business.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching complaints and slamming remedies do not establish selected-parcel broadband coverage or performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the changing-provider complaint guide on 24 July 2023.
The page was last updated on 8 April 2026.
Ofcom notes that millions of people switch phone and broadband provider successfully each year.
Slamming means being switched without knowledge or consent.
A slammed customer should contact the old provider and ask to be switched back.
The customer should also tell the new provider that the switch was not authorised.
The customer should ask the new provider to investigate.
For attempted slamming, the current provider should be asked to cancel the order.
Switching problems should first be raised through the provider's complaint process.
Unresolved switching complaints can proceed to an eligible ADR scheme.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom fines Virgin Media £28m for repeatedly preventing customers from cancelling contracts
guard_streams.write_limit: Enforcement findings about cancellation conduct are provider-behaviour evidence, not selected-parcel coverage or speed evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Virgin Media enforcement outcome on 8 July 2026.
Ofcom fined Virgin Media £28 million.
The findings covered a period of nearly three years.
Ofcom found that millions of calls were likely mishandled.
The conduct prevented or delayed customers from cancelling contracts.
The investigation found deliberate call-dropping tactics.
It found excessive and unnecessary call transfers.
It found customers were repeatedly put on hold without reason.
A commission scheme rewarded call-centre agents for retention-related behaviour.
The conduct created unreasonable difficulty for customers trying to switch to better deals.

guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q3 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rates are service-quality indicators and cannot verify physical network serviceability or selected-parcel performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q3 2025 complaints update on 19 February 2026.
The page was last updated on 8 May 2026.
The figures cover July to September 2025.
Complaints across broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV stayed at similar levels to the previous quarter.
EE, TalkTalk and Vodafone generated the most broadband complaints.
Plusnet generated the fewest broadband complaints.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about landline provider.
Utility Warehouse generated the fewest landline complaints.
O2, Sky Mobile and Three generated the most mobile complaints.
Complaint handling, faults, service and connection issues were leading complaint drivers for the worst mobile performers.

guard_streams.source: Enforcement programme: Industry's failure to implement One Touch Switch by deadline of 3 April 2023
guard_streams.write_limit: Switching enforcement and compliance monitoring do not establish broadband availability, orderability or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom opened the One Touch Switch enforcement programme on 3 April 2023.
Ofcom closed the programme on 11 June 2026.
The relevant rules are General Conditions C7.18 to C7.27.
Industry failed to implement the process by the 3 April 2023 deadline.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer's new provider organises the switch.
One Touch Switch launched for most customers on 12 September 2024.
Ofcom monitored provider matching performance after launch.
Ofcom issued a formal information request in January 2025 about matching issues.
Ofcom concluded that most customers were switching successfully through the process.
Ofcom said it would continue to monitor industry-wide compliance.
